name.evidence: p1 red label: 'CERTAIN ISLANDS & LANDS IN CALIFORNIA GRANT, JOSE Y. LIMANTOUR CLAIMANT'; stamped PAGE 5 petition claims four tracts: First the Farallones, 'Second. The Island called Alcatraces', Third Yerba Buena island, Fourth Punta del Tiburon. 'Alcatraz' names only one of four tracts in the case; Hoffman's 'Islands of Farrallones' is likewise partial.

year.evidence: Stamped PAGE 6 petition: grant 'bearing date on the 16th day of December A.D. 1843'; District Court opinion stamped PAGE 408: 'that of the 16th December (the islands grant) has an approval dated March 1st 1844'. Purported grant dated 1843 (adjudged forged).

governor.evidence: Stamped PAGE 6 petition: grant 'under the authority of the Mexican Government by Manuel Micheltorena Governor of the Californias'; DC opinion stamped PAGE 405 discusses 'the certificate of Micheltorena'. (Grant adjudged forged.)

grantee.evidence: p1 red label and transcript title (stamped PAGE 1): 'Jose Y. Limantour, Claimant'; stamped PAGE 5 petition of Jose Yves Limantour claiming in fee by virtue of the grant made to him. Grantee = claimant here by design of the purported grant.

land_case.evidence: p1 red label 'CASE NO. 429 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; stamp '429 ND' on every leaf; filename cubanc_lcf_nd429.pdf. Commission docket 549 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1).

outcome.evidence: Board opinion 'confirming the claim' Jan 12 1856 (stamped PAGE 4), but District Court opinion (stamped pp. 397-413) finds the Limantour titles forged: 'the forged rubric of Pablo de la Guerra... papers which... could not have been prepared for any honest purpose' (PAGE 410); 'the proofs of fraud in these cases have the force and certainty of a demonstration' (PAGE 410); 'these cases are without parallel in the judicial history of the Country' (PAGE 412). Register 'Rejected' matches the DC disposition, which supersedes the Board.

notes: This is the Limantour fraud case (Commission No. 549 / ND 429, companion to No. 548/ND 424 for the SF pueblo lands). hoffman_1862 'confirmed' reflects only the Board's Jan 1856 decision; the District Court opinion in the file demonstrates fraud and the claim was rejected. Formal decretal page of rejection not among pages read (sits in unread middle pages 41-409); the opinion text is decisive. Register name 'Alcatraz' isolates one of the four tracts claimed; Hoffman's table calls the same docket 'the Islands of Farrallones' - both partial names for the same multi-tract case.

governor.evidence: First grant signed 'Jose Figueroa' as 'Gefe Supr. Politico' (stamped PAGES 31-33; original title stamped PAGES 80-82). Two-league ampliacion decreed 'Febrero 6 de 1836... El S. D. Nicolas Gutierrez Gefe Politico interino de esta Alta California asi lo mando decreto e firmo - Nicolas Gutierres' (stamped PAGES 38-39). Both register governors verified against decrees.

grantee.evidence: Title, stamped PAGE 32 (and original, PAGE 80): 'Por cuanto D. notes: PDF label leaf says 'LAND CASE 79 SD page 131'. name.evidence: p1 red label 'BOSQUEJO GRANT, PETER LASSON CLAIMANT'; transcript title (stamped PAGE 1) 'for the place named Bosquejo'; DC final decree (stamped PAGE 98): 'the land heretofore confirmed to Peter Lassen, known as Bosquejo'.

outcome.evidence: Board opinion 'Confirmed', filed 24 July 1855 (stamped PAGE 58); DC decree of confirmation to Lassen filed 2 Mar 1857 and made final decree by order 29 July 1857 (recited stamped PAGE 96); Henry Gerke, Lassen's grantee, substituted 30 Nov 1859 after Lassen's death (stamped PAGES 92-93); FINAL DECREE 5 Feb 1861: land 'containing... 22,206 22/100 acres... finally confirmed to the said Henry Gerke - Ogden Hoffman' (stamped PAGES 96-99).

notes: Nonstandard PDF filename cubanc00007236_ae_a.pdf (record page lists only volume _a; not multi-volume as downloaded). name.evidence: p1 red label 'BUENA VISTA GRANT'; transcript title (stamped PAGE 1) 'for the place named Buena Vista'; expediente exhibit A titled 'Posecion del rancho de Buenavista' (stamped PAGE 8).

year.evidence: Sola's decree: petition dated 'Presidio de Monterrey... Mayo 28 de 1822', decree same date - 'pongase en posecion de los dos sitios de Ganado mayor y caballar nombrados Buenavista a Dn. Jose Santiago Estrada... firme yo Don Pablo Vicente de Sola' (stamped PAGES 9-10). Regranted by Arguello 10 June 1823, juridical possession 11 June 1823 (stamped PAGES 10-11).

governor.evidence: Register says only 'a Spanish governor'; the decree names him: 'yo Don Pablo Vicente de Sola, Gobernador politico y Militar de esta provincia de la Alta California' (stamped PAGE 10); regrant by 'Don Luis Antonio Arguello... Gefe Superior Politico y Militar', Monterrey 10 June 1823 (stamped PAGE 10). Estrada's own affidavit: '28th day of May A.D. 1822 Pablo Vicente de Sola the then Governor of upper California made and executed to him a Grant' (stamped PAGE 47).

grantee.evidence: Original grantee is Jose Santiago Estrada alone: Sola decree 'pongase en posecion... a Dn. Jose Santiago Estrada' (stamped PAGE 10); his 1822 petition signed 'Jose Santiago Estrada' (stamped PAGE 9). Mariano Malarin is the U.S.-era attorney/claimant (p1 red label 'MARIANO MALARIN, ATTORNEY, CLAIMANT') who later bought part of the land (petition, stamped PAGE 4). Register leads with the claimant; the true grantee appears only inside the attorney formula.

land_case.evidence: p1 red label 'CASE NO. 204 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every leaf stamped '204 SD'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd204.pdf. Commission docket No. 153 (stamped PAGES 1-2).

outcome.evidence: Board: 'Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the Opinion of the Board confirming the claim', 26 Sept 1854 (stamped PAGE 3). District Court: stipulation filed 14 Jan 1857 'that the appeal be dismissed and that the claimant have leave to proceed upon the Decree of the Land Commissioners heretofore rendered in his favor' (stamped PAGES 36-37). Estrada's 1860 affidavit further recites 'the Decree of the United States District Court affirming the Decree of the said Board' (stamped PAGE 49). Confirmation verified.

corrections.governor: Pablo Vicente de Sola (grant 28 May 1822), regranted by Luis Antonio Arguello (10 June 1823) - stamped PAGES 9-10
corrections.grantee: Jose Santiago Estrada, per Sola's decree stamped PAGE 10; Malarin was attorney-claimant

notes: 1860 bill-of-review affidavits (stamped PAGES 38-50) show the confirmed SURVEY was located on the wrong (south) side of the Salinas River per the Estradas; Surveyor General certificate of publication (stamped PAGE 51, issued 27 Apr 1867) says rancho 'confirmed to M. Malarin', survey approved 19 Sept 1859. Register patent fields (patent 15 Sept 1869 to Malarin as attorney) are Phase C. Petition frames the 1822 Sola grant as 'granted under the Mexican Government' (stamped PAGE 4) even though Sola was the Spanish-appointed governor - era label 'spanish' is a judgment call, May 1822 is after Mexican independence.

name.evidence: Bancroft catalogs this case file (digicoll record 269007) as 'Canada de los Pinos (also called College Rancho...) Case no. 388 SD'. The College tracts are claimed inside it per Jimeno deposition stamped pp.89-90 (six sitios of the vacant lands of Mission Santa Ynes embracing the canadas of Sotonocomu, Alisguey and Aguichum, plus two more sitios: San Ysidro, Zanja de Cota). NOTE: the red label (image 1) and transcript title (stamped p.1) name the case 'Lands and Property of the Catholic Church', commission docket 609 - the College Rancho is one property within that omnibus church claim.

year.evidence: Jimeno deposition stamped p.89: 'In the month of March 1844, the Rev. Bishop appointed 3 clergymen to ask... the land necessary for the erection of the College'; p.90: 'in compliance with the petitions the order was made by Governor Micheltorena that the said titles should be issued'. Caveat: the title exhibits themselves (Nos. 3 and 4 A.F., annexed to Bonilla deposition at transcript p.46) were not read; grade rests on Jimeno's sworn identification of them.

governor.evidence: Jimeno dep. stamped pp.89-90: petition 'to Governor Don Manuel Micheltorena'; 'the order was made by Governor Micheltorena that the said titles should be issued'; Q43 (p.90) authenticates Micheltorena's writing on the titles.

grantee.evidence: Jimeno dep. stamped p.90: Exhibit No 3 A.F. is 'the title to the six sitios de ganado mayor... and at the end the acceptance by the Bishop Francisco Garcia Diego'; p.91: the second title's acceptance was by Padre Gonzalez acting for the bishopric after Garcia Diego's death. The original 1844 grantee was Bishop Francisco Garcia Diego (for the ecclesiastical college), NOT Joseph S. Alemany, who is the U.S.-era claimant (red label image 1: 'JOSEPH S. ALEMANY CLAIMANT') and later patentee. Classic claimant-recorded-as-grantee error.

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1: 'CASE No. 388 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every leaf stamped '388 SD'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd388.pdf. Commission docket was 609 (transcript stamped p.1).

outcome.evidence: Board decree of confirmation signed Felch/Thompson/Farwell, 'Filed in Office Dec. 18, 1855' (stamped p.335); U.S. appealed (Ord petition, stamped pp.339-341), then stipulation stamped p.347 (filed 22 March 1858): 'the appeal... be dismissed... and that claimant have leave to proceed under the said decision of the United States Land Commission, heretofore rendered in his favor as under a Final Decree.' Confirmation final. Patent (claimed Feb 28 1861) not in pages read - Phase C checks GLO.

corrections.grantee: Bishop Francisco Garcia Diego (y Moreno), who accepted the 1844 Micheltorena titles for the college (Jimeno dep. stamped pp.90-91); Alemany is the claimant/patentee only.

notes: Omnibus case: commission docket 609 'Lands and Property of the Catholic Church' covering all mission church properties statewide plus the College Rancho tracts; SD court docket 388. Decree pages 317-326 (College-tract description within the decree) not read; decree tail pp.327-335 read. Register's docket SD 388 matches Bancroft's catalog title for the Canada de los Pinos file, so docket linkage is right even though the case label is broader.

name.evidence: Red label image 1: 'LA CANADA DE RINCON GRANT'; transcript title stamped p.1: 'La Canada del Rincon'; Pico title translation stamped p.25: 'a tract of land known by the name of the Canada del Rincon, where the river San Lorenzo runs, in the vicinity of the Mission of Sta Cruz'. Register's long form matches the grant's own description.

year.evidence: 1843 is only the PROVISIONAL title: Micheltorena marginal decree stamped p.14 (translation p.22): 'Angeles July 10th 1843... I give this to the party interested to serve him as a provisional title'. The grant proper is Pico's, 21 April 1846: decree stamped p.16 ('Angeles Abril 21 de 1846... se declara... Pedro Sainsevain dueno en propiedad de la canada de del Rincon'); Board opinion stamped p.29: 'The grant in this case was made on the 21st of April A.D. 1846, & confirmed by the Departmental Assembly on the 10th day of June A.D. 1846'.

governor.evidence: 'Micheltorena; Pico' matches both stages: Micheltorena provisional title 10 July 1843 (stamped p.14, signed 'Micheltna'); Pio Pico definitive title 21 April 1846 (stamped pp.16-17, signed 'Pio Pico, Gobernador Constitucional').

grantee.evidence: Pico decree stamped p.16: 'se declara al Ciudadano Mejicano por naturalizacion Pedro Sainsevain dueno en propiedad de la canada de del Rincon'; red label: 'PEDRO SAINSEVAIN CLAIMANT' (grantee = claimant here).

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1: 'CASE No. 391 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; leaves stamped '391 SD'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd391.pdf. Commission docket 283; the U.S. appeal ran in the NORTHERN District as case No. 90 (land north of 37th parallel, stipulation stamped p.49).

outcome.evidence: Board confirmed: docket stamped p.3 ('Jan 17, 1854... Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the Opinion of the Board confirming the claim'), opinion at stamped pp.29-32. ND District Court decree, Stated Term September 20th 1855 (stamped pp.46-47, Ogden Hoffman Jr.): U.S. filed no notice to prosecute, 'ordered and decreed that the said appeal be dismissed'. SD court dismissed the duplicate U.S. petition 9 Feb 1858 (stamped p.44, Ogier). Confirmation final. Patent (claimed June 4 1858) not in file - Phase C checks GLO.

corrections.year: 1846 (grant by Pico 21 April 1846, Board opinion stamped p.29); 1843 was Micheltorena's provisional title only (10 July 1843, stamped p.14). If the register wants one year for the grant, it should be 1846.

notes: Two-stage grant: 1843 provisional (Micheltorena; full title withheld because Sainsevain was not yet naturalized), naturalization 7 Oct 1844, definitive title 21 Apr 1846 (Pico), Assembly approval 10 June 1846. 1857 Boole affidavits (stamped pp.53-59) attack the claim as inside Pueblo of Santa Cruz limits, but they post-date the final ND decree of 20 Sept 1855.
